arabic_blocks: [906] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني سالم بن عبد الله أن عبد الله بن عمر قال أخذ عمر جبة من إستبرق تباع في السوق فأخذها فأتى رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله ابتع هذه تجمل بها للعيد والوفود، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ إنما هذه لباس من لا خلاق له فلبث عمر ما شاء الله أن يلبث ثم أرسل إليه رسول الله ﷺ بجبة ديباج فأقبل بها عمر فأتى بها رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله إنك قلت: إنما هذه لباس من لا خلاق له وأرسلت إلي بهذه الجبة، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ تبيعها أو تصيب بها حاجتك
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said:

‘Umar took a robe of thick silk that was being sold in the market. He took it and came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, buy this and adorn yourself with it for Eid and for delegations.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘This is only the clothing of one who has no share.’ ‘Umar remained as long as Allah willed him to remain. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent him a robe of silk brocade. ‘Umar came with it and brought it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, you said, “This is only the clothing of one who has no share,” yet you have sent me this robe.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘Sell it, or meet your need with it.’
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The selected text and both Arabic prints say Eid, للعيد. Bewley’s body says the day of Jumu‘a; that comparison wording is not adopted. The pinned Khan-family body agrees on Eid but says bought where the selected opening says took; both occurrences of took remain in the working English.

The two cloth terms, repeated no-share statement, interval as Allah willed, five selected Prophet honorifics and sale-or-need alternatives remain. The comparisons’ explanatory Hereafter wording is not inserted into the selected no-share clause.

The modern print matches the selected chapter’s singular فيه; Brill’s title has فيهما. Brill names ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab at the report opening and includes بها at the first arrival; those longer forms are not inserted. Modern printed reference 948; English bodies Bewley 906 and pinned EPUB 2.15.69.

arabic_blocks: [907] حدثنا أحمد قال: حدثنا ابن وهب قال: أخبرنا عمرو أن محمد بن عبد الرحمن الأسدي حدثه عن عروة عن عائشة قالت دخل علي رسول الله ﷺ وعندي جاريتان تغنيان بغناء بعاث فاضطجع على الفراش وحول وجهه ودخل أبو بكر فانتهرني، وقال مزمارة الشيطان عند النبي ﷺ فأقبل عليه رسول الله عليه السلام، فقال دعهما فلما غفل غمزتهما فخرجتا وكان يوم عيد يلعب السودان بالدرق والحراب فإما سألت النبي ﷺ وإما قال تشتهين تنظرين فقلت: نعم فأقامني وراءه خدي على خده وهو يقول "دونكم يا بني أرفدة" حتى إذا مللت قال حسبك قلت: نعم قال: فاذهبي
english_blocks: Ahmad related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: ‘Amr informed us that Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asadi related to him, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah. She said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while two girls were with me, singing the songs of Bu‘ath. He lay down on the bed and turned his face away. Abu Bakr came in and rebuked me, saying, ‘A pipe of Satan in the presence of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace!’ The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, turned towards him and said, ‘Leave them both.’ When he became inattentive, I signalled to the two of them, and they went out.

It was an Eid day, and the Black people were playing with shields and spears. Either I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or he said, ‘Would you like to watch?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He stood me behind him, my cheek against his cheek, while he was saying, ‘Carry on, Banu Arfidah!’ When I grew tired, he said, ‘Is that enough for you?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Then go.’
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: Both linked accounts remain one complete selected entry, with a paragraph break at وكان يوم عيد. The modern print separately numbers these portions 949 and 950; Brill and the selected digital source join them. Ibn Hajar explicitly records that some transmitters combine the accounts and others separate them. No new app reference or duplicate entry is created.

The source’s uncertainty—either I asked or he offered—both yes replies, cheek-to-cheek wording, Banu Arfidah address and final departure remain. No narrator uncertainty is resolved by selecting a different route.

Three ﷺ symbols and the different written عليه السلام formula are translated separately; the shorter peace formula is not expanded. The singular pipe expression remains singular; source 909 has a distinct plural expression.

Ahmad remains unexpanded, as in the modern print; Brill supplies ibn ‘Isa and an ‘A’ishah honorific absent from the selected text. Girls is the working rendering of جاريتان; the comparisons differ over girls versus slavegirls. No inferred ownership, names, historical battle explanation or ruling on singing is inserted. The selected السودان description is retained rather than replaced with the Abyssinian designation of other routes.
English bodies Bewley 907 and pinned EPUB 2.15.70 both cover the two selected portions. The complete Arabic and all selected words remain unchanged.

arabic_blocks: [908] حدثنا حجاج قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني زبيد قال: سمعت الشعبي عن البراء قال: سمعت النبي ﷺ يخطب، فقال إن أول ما نبدأ من يومنا هذا أن نصلي ثم نرجع فننحر فمن فعل فقد أصاب سنتنا .
english_blocks: Hajjaj related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Zubayd informed me. He said: I heard al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’. He said:

I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delivering a sermon. He said, ‘The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then return and sacrifice. Whoever does that has followed our practice.’

arabic_blocks: [909] حدثنا عبيد بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا أبو أسامة عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت دخل أبو بكر وعندي جاريتان من جواري الأنصار تغنيان بما تقاولت الأنصار يوم بعاث قالت وليستا بمغنيتين، فقال أبو بكر أمزامير الشيطان في بيت رسول الله ﷺ وذلك في يوم عيد، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: "يا أبا بكر إن لكل قوم عيدا وهذا عيدنا".
english_blocks: ‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her. She said:
Abu Bakr came in while two girls from among the girls of the Ansar were with me, singing what the Ansar had said to one another on the day of Bu‘ath.
She said: They were not singers.

Abu Bakr said, ‘Pipes of Satan in the house of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ It was an Eid day. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Abu Bakr, every people has an Eid, and this is our Eid.’

arabic_blocks: [910] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الرحيم حدثنا سعيد بن سليمان قال: حدثنا هشيم قال: أخبرنا عبيد الله بن أبي بكر ابن أنس عن أنس قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ لا يغدو يوم الفطر حتى يأكل تمرات، وقال مرجأ بن رجاء حدثني عبيد الله قال: حدثني أنس عن النبي ﷺ ويأكلهن وترا
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. Sa‘id ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Anas informed us, from Anas. He said:
The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not go out in the morning on the day of Fitr until he had eaten some dates.
Murajja’ ibn Raja’ said: ‘Ubaydullah related to me. He said: Anas related to me, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: He would eat them in an odd number.

arabic_blocks: [911] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا إسماعيل عن أيوب عن محمد عن أنس قال: قال النبي ﷺ من ذبح قبل الصلاة فليعد فقام رجل، فقال هذا يوم يشتهي فيه اللحم وذكر من جيرانه فكأن النبي ﷺ صدقه قال وعندي جذعة أحب إلي من شاتي لحم فرخص له النبي ﷺ فلا أدري أبلغت الرخصة من سواه أم لا
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Anas. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Whoever slaughtered before the prayer must do it again.’ A man stood and said, ‘This is a day on which meat is desired,’ and he mentioned some of his neighbours. It was as though the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, accepted his statement. He said, ‘I have a young she-goat dearer to me than two sheep for meat.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, allowed it for him.
I do not know whether the permission extended to anyone other than him or not.

arabic_blocks: [912] حدثنا عثمان قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن الشعبي عن البراء بن عازب رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال خطبنا النبي ﷺ يوم الأضحى بعد الصلاة، فقال من صلى صلاتنا ونسك نسكنا فقد أصاب النسك ومن نسك قبل الصلاة فإنه قبل الصلاة ولا نسك له، فقال أبو بردة بن نيار خال البراء يا رسول الله فإني نسكت شاتي قبل الصلاة وعرفت أن اليوم يوم أكل وشرب وأحببت أن تكون شاتي أول ما يذبح في بيتي فذبحت شاتي وتغديت قبل أن آتي الصلاة قال شاتك شاة لحم قال: يا رسول الله فإن عندنا عناقا لنا جذعة هي أحب إلي من شاتين أفتجزي عني قال: نعم ولن تجزي عن أحد بعدك
english_blocks: ‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the day of Adha after the prayer. He said, ‘Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice has fulfilled the sacrifice. Whoever sacrifices before the prayer has done so before the prayer, and has no sacrifice.’ Abu Burdah ibn Niyar, al-Bara’s maternal uncle, said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I sacrificed my sheep before the prayer. I knew that today was a day of eating and drinking, and I wanted my sheep to be the first thing slaughtered in my house. So I slaughtered my sheep and ate my midday meal before coming to the prayer.’ He said, ‘Your sheep is a sheep for meat.’ He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, we have a young she-goat that is dearer to me than two sheep. Will it suffice for me?’ He said, ‘Yes, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

arabic_blocks: [913] حدثنا سعيد بن أبي مريم قال: حدثنا محمد بن جعفر قال: أخبرني زيد عن عياض بن عبد الله بن أبي سرح عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ يخرج يوم الفطر والأضحى إلى المصلى فأول شيء يبدأ به الصلاة ثم ينصرف فيقوم مقابل الناس والناس جلوس على صفوفهم فيعظهم ويوصيهم ويأمرهم فإن كان يريد أن يقطع بعثا قطعه أو يأمر بشيء أمر به ثم ينصرف قال أبو سعيد فلم يزل الناس على ذلك حتى خرجت مع مروان وهو أمير المدينة في أضحى أو فطر فلما أتينا المصلى إذا منبر بناه كثير بن الصلت فإذا مروان يريد أن يرتقيه قبل أن يصلي فجبذت بثوبه فجبذني فارتفع فخطب قبل الصلاة فقلت له غيرتم والله، فقال أبا سعيد قد ذهب ما تعلم فقلت: ما أعلم والله خير مما لا أعلم، فقال إن الناس لم يكونوا يجلسون لنا بعد الصلاة فجعلتها قبل الصلاة
english_blocks: Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Zayd informed me, from ‘Iyad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would go out on the day of Fitr and Adha to the prayer ground. The first thing he began with was the prayer. Then he would turn and stand facing the people, while they remained seated in their rows. He would admonish them, counsel them and give them instructions. If he wished to dispatch a force, he dispatched it, or to order something, he ordered it. Then he would leave.

Abu Sa‘id said: The people continued in this way until I went out with Marwan, who was the governor of Madinah, on Adha or Fitr. When we reached the prayer ground, there was a pulpit built by Kathir ibn al-Salt. Marwan wanted to climb it before praying. I pulled at his garment, and he pulled me. He went up and delivered the sermon before the prayer. I said to him, ‘By Allah, you have changed things.’ He said, ‘Abu Sa‘id, what you know has gone.’ I said, ‘By Allah, what I know is better than what I do not know.’ He said, ‘The people would not remain seated for us after the prayer, so I placed it before the prayer.’

arabic_blocks: [918] وعن جابر بن عبد الله قال: سمعته يقول إن النبي ﷺ قام فبدأ بالصلاة ثم خطب الناس بعد فلما فرغ نبي الله ﷺ نزل فأتى النساء فذكرهن وهو يتوكأ على يد بلال وبلال باسط ثوبه يلقي فيه النساء صدقة قلت لعطاء أترى حقا على الإمام الآن أن يأتي النساء فيذكرهن حين يفرغ قال إن ذلك لحق عليهم وما لهم أن لا يفعلوا
english_blocks: And from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah. He said: I heard him say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and began with the prayer, then addressed the people afterwards. When the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had finished, he came down and went to the women and reminded them, leaning on Bilal’s hand. Bilal was spreading out his garment, into which the women were putting charity.
I said to ‘Ata’, ‘Do you consider it a duty for the imam now to go to the women and remind them when he has finished?’ He said, ‘That is indeed a duty upon them. Why should they not do it?’
